d_arms_lint_findings.principle: advisory findings on the existing D1-D4 artifacts (does not block them; surfaces any residual over-claim).

fixtures_passed.principle: each synthetic fixture (clean/circular/no-headroom/naive-SC/no-CI) fires the expected severity (the test evidence).

inference_substrate.principle: aggregation_from_upstream_artifacts (reads artifacts + runs a lint; no LLM).

preconditions_checked.principle: records adversarial_verify-importable check; a missing module emits blocked_.

rules_implemented.principle: the (a)-(e) rule list -- the mechanical contract enforcing oracle-distinctness + headroom-control + paired-CI on moat claims.

flags.detail: Moat/verifier-value claim has verifier_is_oracle=True. Every verifier-moat / beats-SC / verifier_value_added claim must declare verifier_is_oracle=False; missing or true is circular and headline-ineligible.

Moat claim compares against naive self-consistency rather than a TUNED-SC baseline. Add tuned_sc_accuracy / tuned_self_consistency evidence before using the result as a headroom-controlled moat claim.
Positive beats-SC/moat win lacks paired significance evidence: require paired_ci95 and mcnemar_p before a delta>0 headline can be cited.
Null/moat-retirement claim is uninformative because headroom_present is not declared true. A no-headroom corpus cannot support 'does not beat SC' or 'moat retired' as a moat bound.

Positive beats-SC/moat win lacks a valid headroom_present=True anchor (headroom_present is not declared true; positive deltas: delta_vs_tuned_sc=0.12). A win needs oracle@K - tuned_sc >= 0.10 and flips>0 when those fields are present.

rules_implemented.contract: verifier-moat / beats-SC / verifier_value_added claims require verifier_is_oracle=False.
positive delta wins require headroom_present=True with oracle@K - tuned_sc >= 0.10 and flips>0 when those fields are present.
naive self-consistency comparisons are not a tuned-SC headroom-control baseline.
positive beats-SC wins require paired_ci95 and mcnemar_p significance evidence.
no-headroom null or moat-retirement claims are uninformative and must not be mislabeled as a moat bound.
